transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

It's just... well, I've been having some thoughts lately that kind of scared me. Scared me enough to finally make an appointment, anyway. I don't want you to think badly of me, but... I just keep thinking it would be such a relief if I just didn't wake up in the morning. 

I haven't tried to hurt myself, I promise! I haven't done anything like that. It's just those thoughts... I hope it's okay that I came in for that. Am I explaining it right?
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?

Well, um... I suppose it's been about four months now. Right around the time my aunt came to live with us. 

I really hope you don't think I'm foolish for waiting this long to say something to a doctor. I just kept hoping I could shake it off, you know? And I really don't want to make a big fuss, because it's not like I sit around thinking about it all day long. I try to stay busy and be helpful at home. But... yes, it's been about four months since they started. 

Is that... does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any changes in the things you enjoy doing over the past four months?

Well, um... I suppose a little bit. I really don't want to sound like I'm just being lazy, doctor, I promise I'm not. But... I used to always look forward to my watercolors, and my dance class, and going walking with the ladies from the neighborhood. 

It's just that lately... I don't know, I just leave my painting things sitting there on the table. I just can't seem to make myself care about doing any of it anymore. I feel awful admitting that, because I know I should be keeping active, and I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or feeling sorry for myself. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Do you still get pleasure from the things you do, even if you don't feel like doing them?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, I try, I really do. Sometimes I'll force myself to pick up a brush, or I'll go along on the walk just so I don't disappoint the ladies. But... it just feels flat. 

I don't get that little spark of joy I used to get when I'd finish a painting, or the fun of chatting during dance class. It's like I'm just going through the motions. I feel terrible saying that, because I know I should be grateful I have these nice things to do, and I don't want to sound unappreciative. 

But no, the pleasure just... isn't there right now. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying my best to explain it properly for you.
Do you often feel guilty about things that happen in your daily life?

Well, um... I suppose I do, yes. I really try to be a good person, doctor, I promise I do. I try to be patient and kind, especially since my aunt moved in. She needs the help, and it's my duty to take care of her.

But sometimes... well, sometimes I get so tired, or I get a little annoyed with her. And then I just feel awful about it. I start thinking I'm a terrible woman, and that I'm bringing shame on my family for not being more grateful that she's here and that I can help her. I know I shouldn't think that way, and I really don't want you to think I'm a bad niece or a bitter person. I just... I feel so guilty for not being better about it all. 

Does that... is that the sort of thing you mean? I hope I'm not overcomplicating things for you.
Do you still enjoy spending time with the ladies from your neighborhood when you go walking with them?

Well, um... I know I mentioned them before, and I really do think they're wonderful ladies. I don't want to sound like I'm turning my back on my friends, doctor, I really don't. 

But... well, I used to just love our walks so much. I'd look forward to them all week. Lately, though... I just can't seem to make myself care about going. I'll see them out the window and I just... I don't feel that urge to join them anymore. It's the same with my watercolors and my dance class. I just leave my painting things sitting there on the table. 

I feel so bad admitting this again, because I know it sounds terrible, like I'm just being lazy or antisocial. I promise I'm usually a very involved person. I just... I hope you understand I'm not trying to be difficult. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have these thoughts of not wanting to wake up or the feeling of guilt and lack of pleasure been consistently present over the past four months, or have they varied in intensity?

Well, um... yes, I suppose it has been about four months now. It really started right around the time my aunt came to live with us. 

I try so hard not to let it get the best of me, doctor, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all day, or that I'm not trying to push through it. But... well, yes, it's been pretty consistent since she moved in. I just haven't been able to shake it. 

I feel terrible saying that out loud because it sounds like I'm blaming my aunt, and I promise I'm not! She's family and I'm glad to help her. I'm just... I'm trying to give you the honest timeline, even if it makes me sound a bit weak. Is that... does that answer what you were asking me? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Oh, um... I really wish I could give you a better answer, doctor. I know I brought up my watercolors and the dance class before, and walking with the ladies... and I used to just look forward to all of that so much. I try to keep at it, I promise I do, because I know I should be staying active. 

But... well, if I'm being completely honest, no. Lately I just... I leave my painting things sitting right there on the table, and I just can't make myself care about going to class or joining the girls or anything anymore. I feel so guilty saying that, like I'm just giving up, and I really don't want you to think I'm not trying. I just... I can't seem to find the fun in them right now, no matter how hard I try to force it. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a more positive answer for you today. I'm really trying my best to be helpful.
Are there any small things that still give you pleasure, like a favorite food or a beautiful sunset?

Well, um... I really do try to notice the little things, doctor, I promise I do. I know how important it is to count your blessings and appreciate a nice sunset or a good meal. I don't want to sound ungrateful for what I have.

But... well, even the small things just don't seem to spark anything for me right now. Like I was saying about my watercolors and my dance class, and walking with the ladies... I used to just love all of that so much. I'd look forward to them. But lately, I just leave my painting things sitting there on the table, and I can't even make myself care about the things that used to make my whole week. 

I feel so awful repeating myself, and I know it's not the answer you're hoping for. I really wish I could say yes, that a nice sunset makes me smile like it used to. I just... I hope you don't think I'm being intentionally difficult or negative. I'm just trying to be completely honest with you. Am I doing okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over the past four months?

Oh, um... well, I don't think so, doctor. I try to make sure I'm still eating, even when I don't have much of an appetite, because I know it's important to keep my strength up. I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm neglecting myself. 

So, no, I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently or anything like that. I step on the scale every now and then just to check, and it seems to be staying right about where it usually is. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, at least that's one thing I'm managing to keep steady, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before these thoughts started?

Oh, um... well, I try to keep my energy up, I really do. I make sure to get out of bed and do what I can, because I don't want to be a burden to anyone. 

But... well, my husband did mention the other day that I move like everything takes extra effort now. I hate to admit it, because I really don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or not trying to push through. But I suppose he's right. Even when I go down to the market, I'll just... I'll stand there for entirely too long before picking up what I came for. I just sort of stall out, I guess, like my body is made of lead. 

I feel so silly even saying it out loud, and I'm so sorry if that sounds like I'm just complaining. I hope I'm explaining it okay for you? I really am trying my best to give you the right answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over the past four months?

Oh, sleep... well, um, I think my sleep has been pretty normal, doctor. I always try to keep a very regular schedule, you know? I make sure to go to bed at a sensible hour because I know how important rest is, and I really wouldn't want to make things worse by staying up all hours of the night. 

So, no, I haven't really noticed any big changes there. I'm still getting my usual amount of rest, just waking up at my normal time. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm doing all the right things, and I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless, or do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to?

Oh, um... I know we just touched on this a moment ago, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm making a fuss. I try so hard to keep busy and not let things slow me down. 

But, well, like I was saying about what my husband noticed... I guess I am moving a bit slower. He says it looks like everything just takes extra effort for me lately. And I hate to admit it, because I really do try to push past it, but even when I'm just at the market, I'll find myself just standing there for entirely too long before I finally pick up the item I went in for. It's not that I'm restless or fidgety, it's more like... I just sort of stall. 

I'm so sorry to repeat myself, doctor. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Are there any activities or things that you used to enjoy, but now feel completely uninterested in?

Well, um... I really do try to keep busy, doctor, because I know it's good for me to stay active. I usually have my little routines... like my watercolors, and my dance class. And I always used to look forward to walking with the ladies from the neighborhood. 

But... oh, I hate to even say it, because I know it makes me sound so lazy... lately I just leave my painting things sitting there on the table. And I haven't been going to class or out for our walks. I just... I can't seem to make myself care right now, no matter how hard I try to force it. 

I feel so guilty admitting that out loud. It sounds terrible, doesn't it? I hope you don't think poorly of me for it, I really am trying to snap out of it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had more than one period of feeling this way in your life?

Oh, um... no, doctor. I really don't think so. I mean, everyone has their little slumps, right? But nothing like this. 

I've always prided myself on being a very steady person, you know? I always try to keep a cheerful home and just... get on with things. So, no, this is really the first time I've ever felt quite this... stuck. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, I hope it's not a bad thing that this is the first time. I just want to be completely honest with you so you can tell me what I need to do to fix it. Am I giving you the right kind of answers?
Have you ever felt this low or had similar thoughts before in your life?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, doctor, I know you just asked something similar a moment ago. I really hope I didn't confuse you with my last answer, it's probably my fault for not being clear enough. 

But, um, no... I really haven't ever felt this low before in my whole life. I've always been the kind of person who just, you know, puts on a brave face and gets the housework done. So feeling this far down, and having these kinds of thoughts... it's all completely new for me. 

I hope that makes sense? Please tell me if I'm not explaining things right, or if you need me to answer it differently. I really just want to make sure I'm being helpful to you.
Have you had any periods in the past where you felt similarly before this four-month stretch?

Oh dear... I am just so sorry, doctor. I must be doing a terrible job of explaining myself today, since you're having to ask me again. I really apologize if I'm making your job harder or if I'm not using the right words. 

But, um... no. Before these last four months started, I never had anything like this happen to me. I've always been right as rain before this, just keeping the house tidy and minding my own business. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything from you, I just... I really haven't ever felt this way before now. 

Is there... did I say something wrong before? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes. I can try to answer differently if that's what you need?
Have you ever had an episode like this before in your life that lasted for a while and then got better on its own?

Oh, my goodness... doctor, I am so terribly sorry. I feel awful that I must be doing this all wrong if you're having to ask me about it again. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or hold anything back from you. 

But... no, I really haven't. Not even something that came and went on its own. I've always just... managed, you know? Kept my head down and took care of my family without any fuss. 

I really hope I'm not ruining your evaluation by giving you the same answer. Am I... am I supposed to have had this happen before? I can try to think really, really hard if you need me to remember something, but I just... I really don't think I have. I'm so sorry if that's not what you were looking for.
Have you ever had another period in your life where you felt similarly to how you've been feeling over the past four months?

Oh, I... I feel just dreadful that we keep coming back to this. I must really be making a mess of things today, and I am so, so sorry if I'm wasting your time. I know you're very busy and I'm probably just not giving you the right kind of information.

But... no, doctor. I really, truly haven't. Before these last few months, I've just been... well, normal, I suppose. Just taking care of the house, looking after things. I never had any kind of spell like this before in my whole life. 

I feel terrible giving you the same answer again. Are you... are you sure I'm doing this right? I really want to be a good patient for you, so please, if I'm doing something wrong, just tell me and I'll try to fix it.
Have you had any other periods in your life where you felt similarly depressed, before these past four months?

Oh, dear me... I am just so embarrassed. You're asking me again, which means I must not be making myself clear at all. I am so sorry, doctor. I know you're just trying to help me, and I'm probably being terribly frustrating.

I... I really haven't ever felt this way before. Never in my whole life until these last four months. I've always been the one taking care of everyone else, keeping everything nice and neat. I've never had a... a spell of feeling so low like this before. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a different answer for you. I'm really not trying to be difficult, I promise. Is it... is it bad that this is the first time it's happened? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers for your report.
